title: A Reactor Held Plasma Over 100 Million Degrees for 1,066 Seconds

scenes.text: A reactor held plasma over 100 million degrees for 1,066 seconds.
That's nearly 18 minutes inside China's EAST tokamak.
The core of the Sun is only about 15 million degrees.
No material can touch plasma that hot. Magnetic fields hold it in a ring.
The previous record was 403 seconds, set by the same machine in 2023.
Several times hotter than the Sun's core, held for 1,066 seconds.

description:
China's EAST tokamak held a plasma at more than 100 million degrees for 1,066 seconds in January 2025.
The previous record was 403 seconds.
Could fusion power your home one day?
first_comment: Will fusion ever power your home?
